title: fix(sessions): avoid repeated host compaction after native compaction
body:
Fixes #168015

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: native Codex auto-compaction clears a matching host transcript byte-fuse latch, causing another host compaction attempt on the next turn even though the host transcript is unchanged.

## User Impact

Oversized sessions avoid the redundant model request, latency, and compaction-start notice after native-only compaction. Current main already continues with bounded history after a failed byte compaction; this change fixes the remaining repeated-preflight defect. Host compaction can still clear or refresh suppression. No configuration, protocol, SDK, schema, or stored-format change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared accounting projection now preserves an omitted latch, sets a supplied value, and treats explicit `null` as clearing intent that survives the metadata-worker JSON boundary. Byte-preflight owners explicitly replace or clear their observation. Completed host rewrites carry a fact through reply, settlement, and direct-command accounting; folding a later native fact cannot erase that host fact. Manual native-only compaction preserves suppression, while manual host compaction clears it.

Maintainer cleanup removes the separate tagged intent type, shares the projection's parameter contract, removes repeated target fields, and simplifies the committed-result return without weakening session/writer authority. Private-state fixtures now use `InternalSessionEntry`.

Original fix by @ruel225; maintainer cleanup and complete consumer cutover by @steipete. Ordinary/follow-up regression coverage incorporates @xydigitLybnnnn's overlapping #168095, with verified human co-author credit in the maintainer commit. That PR remains open pending the coordinator's landing decision.

## Evidence

Candidate: `332fb5cbc565c623cdc5365b563b5137f30be60d`, merged with main `8420f82cbbf8bd0114cacc39fa51299f92851a6f` before final proof. The integrated patch is identical to the independently reviewed candidate.

- Main-projection negative control reproduced on secretless AWS lease `cbx_7b7417047366` (`r7a.xlarge`, 32,135,880 KiB RAM), run `run_0ebe2a667c176b8b0023b57834af29cb`: original contributor tests with only the production projection restored from main `123d5a1331a8307969767b34e8f8808461ea205b` failed with `expected undefined to deeply equal { activeBytes: 60000, … }`. Command: `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-result-accounting.persistence.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'keeps byte-preflight suppression for native-only compaction accounting'`; wall time 44.13 s. Lease released.
- Targeted formatting and oxlint passed after removing an unused test import.
- Independent Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2, no findings. It is source review, not runtime proof.
- Exact-head CI [38047937131](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38047937131) succeeded with 52 successful jobs and 25 skipped jobs, including successful completion of the CI gate, production types, all core test-type shards, and architecture checks.
- Independent AWS proof on `cbx_38c30b9a0192` (`r7a.xlarge`, 32,135,880 KiB RAM): seven changed test files passed **168 tests** in **253.61 s** with `--maxWorkers=1`; `pnpm tsgo:core` passed in **73.71 s**; `pnpm tsgo:core:test --changed-paths-json <the 19 changed paths>` passed all **27 selected graphs** in **1801.46 s**.
- Full production-only negative control: restore all ten changed production files from the integrated main base while retaining the regressions, then `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/session-updates.exec-preparation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'records and clears byte-compaction progress with authoritative accounting'`. It failed at the intended preservation assertion (`expected undefined to deeply equal { activeBytes: 60000, … }`) in **31.59 s**. Candidate source was restored and verified clean before later proof.
- **Real Gateway/native comparison:** secretless lease `cbx_7c7a593a8fc3`, run `run_dbe6ad2955ef966466fc5871eae044fb`, real Codex app-server and QA mock provider. Against main production, native compaction advanced the persisted count and erased the latch; the following real turn logged `trigger=transcript_bytes`. On the restored candidate, native compaction advanced the count to 2 while retaining the latch; the following turn advanced it to 3, returned `LATCH-NEXT-TURN-OK`, retained the latch, and produced **zero byte-preflight triggers**. Baseline flow: **72.83 s**. Both flows used isolated state, ephemeral ports, and synthetic content.
- **Real host rewrite:** fresh secretless lease `cbx_820f0081e9d2`, run `run_b09c63b584f74c15e235c0b27fd2e8c5`, real Gateway with the OpenClaw runtime and QA mock provider. `sessions.compact({key:"agent:qa:main",agentId:"qa"})`, without `maxLines`, made a successful summary request and returned `ok:true, compacted:true`. The persisted host boundary/count changed from 0 to 1 and the latch was cleared. The next real turn returned `LATCH-HOST-NEXT-TURN-OK`, measured **2080 active bytes < 256000**, and did not repeat byte compaction. Host flow: **68.13 s**, owned Gateway cleanup passed.

ClawSweeper revision 7 reviewed this exact head and reports **zero actionable findings**, **complete fix scope**, **sufficient real-behavior proof**, and **no before-merge requests**. Its previous direct-command, private-fixture-type, manual-host, and automatic-host findings are resolved.

The initial whole-directory invocation passed 124 files in its first two groups, then exhausted an unchanged 512 MiB SQLite worker heap during the long-lived Gateway group, producing repeated native-retirement errors in untouched usage tests. It was stopped and its lease released. That original memory failure is retained as unresolved evidence; no heap profile or retainer analysis was collected, so no leak classification or fix is claimed. The complete **1472-file CI-safe inventory finished successfully** in **62 disjoint batches** of at most 24 explicit paths through the unchanged `pnpm test <paths...>` runner. Each batch used a fresh process and the original heap/timeout limits; every batch exited 0. Final totals: **1468 files passed, 4 files skipped; 19,153 tests passed, 21 skipped**. Inventory reconciliation found no missing or duplicated paths. This passing bounded replay does not establish a fix for the original memory failure.

The four skipped files are existing opt-in benchmarks: `session-entry-snapshots.benchmark.test.ts`, `sessions-list-cold.benchmark.test.ts`, `sessions-list-worker.benchmark.test.ts`, and `system-info.benchmark.test.ts`; their source guards require benchmark-specific environment flags. No regression was disabled.

These are same-head, fresh `r7a.xlarge` leases, with one command at a time per lease. Total batch wall time summed across lanes: **15,178.59 s**. Coverage includes the whole changed module directories and outside test importers. Run IDs: `run_8d84fd8c533fc79949b74096134f6689`, `run_edba83c2417627e3b51d3190be421d88`, `run_6d686c282b098981fb58ded7d905b53a`, and `run_adcb778623a377b955f44f075d42288e`.

The existing `sessions-create.visible-spawn.live.test.ts` additionally requires live-test enablement and a real provider credential and is outside this secretless run; the required mock-provider Gateway proof is documented above.

The first broad-run failure was the untouched `dispatch-from-config.verbose-worker.test.ts`, reproduced separately on full current main `bfe58537cadc92d945e053406942a600a96b37c0` on lease `cbx_138ce629bdf7` (**46.26 s**):

```sh
pnpm test:unit:fast \
  src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.commentary.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.verbose-worker.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism --no-cache --sequence.shuffle=false
```

The commentary suite's shared harness leaves a mocked session reader returning `verboseLevel:"off"`; the next shared-worker SQLite test therefore misses its foreign update to `full`. The same test passed alone on main in 40.16 s; that passing replay is not a fix. The separate repair belongs in test routing, alongside the already excluded dispatch mock suites. No production guard or test weakening was added here.

```sh

  node scripts/prepare-vitest-runtime.mjs --require-current-head
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/tsdown-build.mts --config tsdown.ai.config.ts
```

Task-owned standalone fixtures reused `createQaGatewayChild`, the QA bus, and `startQaMockOpenAiServer`; they ran with Node assertions and isolated HOME/state/config under the task namespace:

```sh
OPENCLAW_LATCH_EXPECT_BASELINE=1 bash run-standalone.sh baseline /private/tmp/oc-r7-latch
OPENCLAW_LATCH_EXPECT_BASELINE=0 bash run-standalone.sh fixed /private/tmp/oc-r7-latch
bash run-host-compaction.sh host-compaction /private/tmp/oc-r7-latch
```

The baseline restored only the ten production files from main; the candidate restored them from HEAD and rebuilt. The native fixture required an observed native event plus durable accounting before checking the next turn. Its first 64 KB version did not reach native compaction after a native rollout reset; the revised 256 KB fixture permits one additional real thread-establishing turn and still requires the event. The initial Vitest baseline attempt hit its no-output watchdog. These were fixture failures, not passing product proof.

The combined native script's later host phase was not counted as passing: the forced-Codex QA configuration redirects native app-server traffic to the mock while leaving the generic host summarizer's catalog URL unchanged. The separate fully mocked OpenClaw `sessions.compact` cell above proves actual host summary, persistence, invalidation, and shrink. No real provider credentials were used, and no operator Gateway/state was touched.

</details>

Original-head CI run `38039413693` failed on the private-latch fixture types addressed here. Its unrelated Kysely guard failures in `src/state/openclaw-migration-witness.ts` and dashboard pin click failures were separately repaired on main by `db6449d3f609` and `dd036a4b1d85`; both are included in this candidate. No failed job is relabeled as passing.
